gold.verbatim: published in the Journal of Metabolic Medicine on 4 September 2023
time-restricted eating produced a modest improvement in glycaemic control among adults with prediabetes
Time-restricted eating is a pattern in which all daily calories are consumed within a fixed window
The trial enrolled 218 participants aged between 34 and 67
recruited from four clinics in Ontario
Mean HbA1c fell by 0.31 percentage points in the intervention group against 0.08 in the control group
The difference of 0.23 points was statistically significant at p = 0.004
Fasting insulin fell by 12% in the intervention group
84% of intervention participants met the eight-hour window on at least six days a week
by week 26 that figure had fallen to 51%
Nineteen participants withdrew, eleven of them citing social difficulty in keeping to the schedule
said Dr. Priya Raghunathan, the trial's principal investigator
The trial was funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research
Two of the eleven authors declared consulting fees from a manufacturer of continuous glucose monitors
the 26-week duration is too short to establish whether the improvement persists
